summary:
FieldShift is an interactive crop-rotation and soil-resilience decision-support web app that turns NASA Earth observations into clear, practical planting guidance for smallholder farmers. It pairs 2001-2025 NASA POWER agroclimatology (MERRA-2 meteorology and CERES/SYN1deg solar data) and GPM IMERG precipitation with NASA GIBS map layers (SMAP L4 surface moisture and Terra MODIS 8-day NDVI), SRTM-referenced slope profiles, 10 m Copernicus Sentinel-2 point checks, and FAO EcoCrop envelopes. Across five study regions (four Philippine basins and a Central Illinois benchmark), it flags seasonal risks like dry-season moisture drops, hillside topsoil runoff, and heavy-rain spray washout.


At the center is the deterministic Farm Adaptation and Resilience Index (FARI), which scores and compares 15 strategies (baseline monocrops against nitrogen-fixing legumes and climate-resilient relays) using farmer priority sliders, drought/heatwave/deluge stress toggles, and a 90-day traffic-light foliar spray and urea risk screen. To avoid over-claiming from orbit, FieldShift caps satellite confidence at 80% and reserves 20% for local soil-kit testing. It includes plain-language and technical modes, voice readouts, copyable SMS briefs, and printable A4 plans to support, never replace, farmer judgment and local agricultural expertise.
details:
FieldShift helps smallholder farmers and local agricultural extension workers turn decades of NASA Earth observations into calm, practical planting and soil-care decisions. For a farming family in Nueva Ecija, Bukidnon, Isabela, or Guimaras, a cropping calendar is tied directly to household food security, production loans, and seasonal weather. Switching an entire field to an unfamiliar crop carries real risk. Rather than asking farmers to abandon what already feeds them, FieldShift compares their existing practice side by side with low-risk, soil-rebuilding rotations and short-duration relays backed by transparent climate evidence.

How It Works

FieldShift follows a clear, grounded rhythm: choose a farm, read the season, set priorities, compare three tailored strategies, and bring a plain-language brief to a local agronomist or cooperative. Across five study locations (four Philippine agricultural basins plus a Central Illinois benchmark farm in the United States), the platform evaluates 15 twelve-month cropping strategies using 2001-2025 NASA POWER agroclimatology baselines (MERRA-2 meteorology and CERES/SYN1deg solar radiation), NASA GPM IMERG rainfall, and SRTM-referenced slope context. In the interactive satellite map, live NASA GIBS WMS layers (SMAP L4 surface soil moisture, Terra MODIS 8-day NDVI, and GPM IMERG precipitation rate) sit alongside a 10 m ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 bare-soil NDVI check and a live 3-day Open-Meteo weather outlook.
At the core of the planner is the deterministic Farm Adaptation and Resilience Index (FARI), which scores each strategy from 0 to 100 across four normalized pillars: Conserve Water (W), Stop Erosion (E), Rebuild Nutrients (N), and Supplemental Income (M). Farmers can adjust priority sliders, toggle practical field constraints (rainfed only, manual tools only, or fast 60-day cash turnaround), and simulate drought, heatwave, and heavy-rain deluge scenarios to see how every crop option holds up before investing in seeds or fertilizer.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Safer Spray and Fertilizer Timing: The 90-Day Climatological Flower Induction (CFI) and Urea Risk Screen evaluates historical storm frequency (>= 14 mm/day), heat stress, and root-zone moisture in simple green, amber, and red windows. For Guimaras mango growers and lowland rice-corn farmers, avoiding poorly timed foliar sprays and top-dressing helps prevent projected agrochemical washout losses of PHP 15,000-35,000/ha and reduces nitrogen runoff into nearby waterways.

- Rebuilding Living Soil Without High Cash Risk: FieldShift models biological nitrogen fixation (+35 to +80 kg N/ha projected range) from 60-day mungbean, peanut, cowpea, and Arachis pintoi relays, highlighting a 25-40% projected reduction in synthetic urea alongside livestock forage utility and open-pollinated (OPV) farmer-saved seed options.

- Protecting Vulnerable Uplands: Across steep 11% slopes in Bukidnon, contour strips
and living mulches help anchor topsoil during tropical downpours, supporting long-term food security, clean water, and climate resilience.
What Makes It Creative & What Our Team Considered
Most remote-sensing tools either stop at complex maps or claim more from space than satellites can honestly measure. FieldShift was designed around humility and field realism:

1. 80/20 Two-Tier Soil Resilience Certificate: Orbital confidence is strictly capped at 80%. The remaining 20% requires local field-kit testing (subsurface soil pH, plant-available N-P-K, organic matter, and physical inspection), preventing over-claiming where satellites cannot see underground.
2. Five Plain-Language Explanations on Every Strategy: Instead of black-box rankings, every strategy explains Why Suggested, Supporting NASA Evidence, Expected Benefits, Data Gaps, and Local Review Alerts, while clearly badging modeled overlays and literature estimates as "Illustrative / modeled" or "Projected estimate."
3. Built for Real Rural Workflows: Because field conversations happen in local languages and often under weak connectivity, FieldShift supports English, Binisaya, and Tagalog, includes a Plain-English vs. Technical terminology toggle, offers hands-free Web Speech API audio readouts, and creates one-click SMS summaries and printable A4 consultation briefs.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software
FieldShift is built as a strict TypeScript monorepo with two workspaces: @fieldshift/climate-data (pure deterministic calculation engines, 2001-2025 NASA POWER JSON baselines, UN FAO EcoCrop climate envelopes, and PSA/USDA price snapshots with zero DOM dependencies) and @fieldshift/web (React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and Leaflet with Esri World Imagery, OpenStreetMap, and NASA GIBS WMS layers). Scientific invariants and UI guardrails are verified with 43 automated Vitest tests and strict TypeScript typechecking, and the app runs entirely client-side on Vercel with no paid API keys required.
